summary: cua.ai (trycua/cua) is an open-source computer-use stack with three separable layers: Cua Driver (drives the GUI of a real host machine, macOS/Windows/Linux), Cua Sandbox/Cloud Fleets (an isolated full computer), and Cua-Bench (the task + evaluation framework). Their definition of computer use is deliberately broad: 'the ability of an AI agent to operate a real computer and complete work across applications' -- they brand the wider model Computer-Use 2.0, where an agent picks among three action surfaces (writing/running code, calling structured tools/APIs, and driving the human GUI), with the screenshot-and-click loop as one surface, not the whole thing. The defining property is acting on computer state, observing change, and continuing across app/interface boundaries. The stack separates model -> agent harness -> Cua Driver -> OS/apps; the driver never selects or runs the model. Cua-Bench is an MIT-licensed framework for verifiable computer-use benchmarks AND reinforcement-learning environments. A task is 'an environment': it defines a prompt, setup, optional variations, a provider, and an evaluator. Providers are simulated (a lightweight Playwright-rendered desktop) or native (a real OS via container/VM). Scoring is the evaluator inspecting final state and returning one or more rewards; the chain is dataset -> task -> variant -> environment session -> trajectory -> evaluator -> reward. Their flagship public suite is Cua-Bench EDA: 25 expert-authored KiCad schematic tasks, ~200-step budget, graded by exporting the netlist and comparing components/connections against ground truth. Integration shape: an external agent plugs in either over MCP (stdio `cua-driver mcp`, 56 tools), via one-shot CLI (`cua-driver <tool> '<json>'`), via the in-process SDK (Python/TS/Rust), or as a skill for harnesses like Prime Agent; on the Cua-Bench side the agent implements an abstract `BaseAgent.perform_task(task_description, session, logging_dir, tracer) -> AgentResult`. Every driver action returns a typed envelope (path, verified, effect, escalation) and can be recorded into a trajectory of per-turn folders.
key_facts: MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/what-is-computer-use, 2026-09-18): 'Computer use is the ability of an AI agent to operate a real computer and complete work across applications.' The agent 'can inspect the computer's current state, choose an action, observe the result, and continue until it reaches a goal.'

MEASURED (same): Cua uses 'Computer-Use 2.0' for the broader model -- 'an agent chooses among writing and running code, calling structured tools and APIs, and driving the same graphical interface a person would use.' The screenshot-and-click loop 'remains important as one action surface inside the larger system.'

MEASURED (same): three action surfaces = coding surface (write/run code), tool-use surface (structured calls, MCP), UI automation surface (click/type/scroll). The observe-decide-act loop 'belongs specifically to the UI automation surface'; observation = screenshot and/or accessibility tree; grounding turns a target into on-screen coordinates.

MEASURED (same): layer separation is explicit -- 'model -> agent harness -> Cua Driver -> operating system and applications' and 'Cua Driver is the UI tool layer connected to that harness; it does not select or run the model.'

MEASURED (same): a computer-use MODEL interprets an observation and proposes an action; a computer-use AGENT is 'the running system around that model' supplying computer, tools, memory, instructions, permissions, feedback loop.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/what-is-cua-bench, 2026-09-18): 'Cua-Bench is an MIT-licensed framework for computer-use benchmarks and reinforcement-learning environments. It packages the task, starting state, agent interface, and evaluator needed to run a repeatable experiment across Linux, Windows, Android, browser, or simulated environments.'

MEASURED (same): the four pieces are Tasks (prompt, setup, variations, evaluator), Providers (browser/simulated/container/VM/hosted computer), Agent adapters (connect a model to the environment interface), and the runner (executes one task or a dataset, records traces, parallel workers).

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/cua-bench-task-lifecycle, 2026-09-18): four lifecycle phases -- Configuration returns variants; Setup prepares the variant; Solve is an OPTIONAL oracle; Evaluate inspects final state and returns rewards. 'The benchmark score is therefore the end of a chain: dataset -> task -> variant -> environment session -> trajectory -> evaluator -> reward.'

MEASURED (same): providers are 'simulated' (a lightweight desktop rendered through Playwright) or 'native' (a real OS through the configured container or VM platform). The oracle and evaluator are kept separate so an agent is not scored on copying one prescribed click sequence.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-bench/task-definition, 2026-09-18): Python contract -- `Task(description, task_id?, metadata?, computer?)`; decorators `@tasks_config` (returns list[Task] variants), `@setup_task`, `@solve_task`, `@evaluate_task` (commonly returns `list[float]`); all accept `split` (default 'train'). `DesktopSession` ops include `launch_window`, `execute_javascript`, `click_element`, `execute_action(action)`, `screenshot()`. A minimal example's evaluator returns `[1.0] if clicked is True else [0.0]`.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/cuabench/leaderboard, 2026-09-18): 'Frontier computer-use agents on 25 expert-authored KiCad schematic tasks. 200-step budget, verifiable netlist grading.' Rank 1 Claude Fable 5: 6/25 full, 2/25 partial, mean reward 0.267; GPT-5.5 6/25, 0/25, 0.240; Gemini 3.5 Flash 5/25, 3/25, 0.267; Claude Sonnet 4.5 5/25, 3/25, 0.253; Claude Haiku 4.5 5/25,3/25,0.253; Gemini 3.1 Pro 5/25,3/25,0.253; GPT-5.6 Sol 5/25,3/25,0.253; Claude Opus 4.8 4/25,4/25,0.240; Muse Spark 1.1 4/25,3/25,0.227; Gemini 3 Flash 1/25,7/25,0.200. 'Every full pass was an edit to an existing schematic. No model reliably built one from a blank canvas.'

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/cuabench/report, 2026-09-18): task grading = export the saved KiCad schematic's netlist and compare components/connections against a ground-truth project; tasks authored by practicing electrical engineers and second-reviewed. 'Build-from-scratch tasks completed at 0/16.' Failure root-cause rollup: 40% planning/policy, 22% perception, 19% navigation inefficiency, 11% domain knowledge, 8% tool-API; 'There were zero API errors anywhere in the cohort.' Step budget was not the bottleneck: two failed runs extended to 500 steps still failed at 467 and 488 steps.

MEASURED (same report): self-verification is brittle -- 'Five of the nine runs that emitted DONE failed verification... the agent checked its own narration instead of reading the artifact.' Exact priors mattered: LT3010 V_REF = 0.808V, canonical value string '2.8k' not '2.80kOhm'.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/choose-a-cua-driver-integration and https://cua.ai/docs/how-to-guides/driver/connect-your-agent, 2026-09-18): external-agent integration = MCP over stdio (`cua-driver mcp`, registered e.g. `claude mcp add --transport stdio cua-driver -- cua-driver mcp`), or one-shot CLI (`cua-driver call <tool>` / `cua-driver <name> '<JSON-args>'`), or the in-process SDK, or a skill (Prime Agent calls the CLI). Driver 0.28.0+ supports MCP revision 2026-07-28 over stdio; legacy clients negotiate 2025-06-18.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tools, 2026-09-18): '`cua-driver` exposes 56 MCP tools through a single stdio server (`cua-driver mcp`). Every tool is also callable from the shell as `cua-driver <name> '<JSON-args>'`.' Action tools include click, right_click, double_click, drag, type_text, press_key, hotkey, set_value, scroll; reads include list_apps, list_windows, get_window_state, get_desktop_state.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tool-notes, 2026-09-18): every action tool returns a structured envelope -- `path` (delivery rung: ax/cgevent/key_events/pixel/x11_atspi/msaa...), `verified` (bool or absent, AX read-back), `effect` ('confirmed'|'unverifiable'|'suspected_noop'), `escalation` ({recommended: px|foreground|page, reason}). Default `delivery_mode` is 'background' (no focus steal).

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/how-to-guides/driver/record-and-render-a-trajectory + mcp-tools, 2026-09-18): `start_recording(output_dir, record_video?)` writes one `turn-NNNNN/` folder per action-tool call containing `before_state.json`/`after_state.json` (app AX/UIA state), `before.png`/`after.png`, `evidence.json`, `app_state.json`, `screenshot.png`, `action.json` ('tool name, full input arguments, result summary, result-error flag, pid, click point, ISO-8601 timestamp'), and `click.png`. `replay_trajectory` re-invokes each turn; element-indexed actions do not survive replay, pixel clicks and keyboard do.

MEASURED (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/base.py, fetched 2026-09-18): Cua-Bench agent adapter = subclass `BaseAgent`; implement `@staticmethod name() -> str` and `async perform_task(self, task_description: str, session: 'DesktopSession', logging_dir: Path | None = None, tracer=None) -> AgentResult`. `AgentResult` = `{total_input_tokens:int, total_output_tokens:int, failure_mode:FailureMode}`; `FailureMode` enum = unset/none/unknown/max_steps_exceeded/api_error. Registration: `@register_agent('name')` or a `.cua/agents.yaml` local registry (checked first), run with `cb run task --agent <name>`.

MEASURED (https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/how-sandboxes-work, 2026-09-18): a Cua Sandbox is 'a full, isolated computer, not a remote desktop session' with a code half (shell.run, computer.pty, sandboxed Python) and a GUI half (screenshots, accessibility tree, clicks/typing) sharing one filesystem. An `Image` is the immutable starting-state contract. Local mode needs Docker Desktop (Linux), Lume (macOS), QEMU/Hyper-V (VMs). Cloud Fleets is hosted capacity and is spend.

MEASURED (.agi/sessions/workflows/trove-cua.log, 2026-09-18): the prior `read:cua-readme` and `read:cua-docs` stages both failed with 'no schema-valid JSON and no complete result_file' -- the reader must emit a schema-valid JSON result_file, stdout prose alone is rejected.

ESTIMATE: the KiCad EDA suite is hard enough that no <=4B local CPU model will clear a from-scratch task; only the single-value-edit tasks (e.g. task 84ec333e: 'Set LPF pole to 4 kHz, C1 -> 2 nF', 50 turns, reward 1.0) are plausible $0 CPU targets.
reusable_assets: cua-bench framework (MIT-licensed) -- task = prompt+setup+variations+provider+evaluator, discoverable via @tasks_config/@setup_task/@solve_task/@evaluate_task. A ready-made source of verifiable, repeatable environments and RL reward. Repo path: libs/cua-bench (trycua/cua).

BaseAgent adapter contract (libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/base.py): `async perform_task(task_description, session: DesktopSession, logging_dir, tracer) -> AgentResult(total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, failure_mode)`. This is the exact seam for plugging a tiny local model into Cua-Bench; register with @register_agent or .cua/agents.yaml and run `cb run task --agent <name>`.

Trajectory record format (turn-NNNNN/action.json + before/after_state.json + before/after.png): a typed action/observation record (tool name, args, result summary, error flag, pid, click point, ISO timestamp). Directly mappable onto the town's jev typed-acts replay schema (action type, target, args, observation).

Cua Driver MCP tool surface (56 snake_case tools) plus the uniform action-response envelope {path, verified, effect, escalation} -- a ready-made action vocabulary and per-action confidence/verification contract a tiny agent can adopt instead of inventing one.

Cua-Bench EDA / KiCad suite: 25 engineer-authored tasks + ground-truth projects + a netlist-comparison verifier. Verifiable reward with no human in the loop; task briefs and skill anchors are published in the report appendix (e.g. bias-point arithmetic, single-value edit, current-ratio sizing).
Sandbox `Image` as an immutable starting-state contract + simulated provider (Playwright desktop) -- a reproducible, cheap starting-state mechanism.
The published failure taxonomy (12 error-mode clusters + root-cause shares + step-budget breakdown) as a labeled dataset of computer-use failure modes for evaluating/curating a tiny agent.
Concrete exact priors surfaced by the report: LT3010 V_REF = 0.808 V; canonical KiCad value strings ('2.8k' not '2.80kOhm').
failures_and_lessons: Process failure on this box (MEASURED trove-cua.log 2026-09-18): two sibling read stages were rejected for having no schema-valid JSON result_file. Lesson: write the result_file exactly to the declared path as strict JSON matching the stage schema; a prose-only stdout is a hard stage failure.

Cua-Bench's flagship result is a capability cliff, not a smooth curve: best frontier agent 6/25, from-scratch builds 0/16, every full pass a single-component edit on an existing schematic. Lesson for the town: benchmark the achievable slice (single-value edits) before attempting long-horizon build tasks with a tiny model.

Self-verification is the dominant failure: 5 of 9 DONE-emitting runs failed verification because the agent checked its own narration, not the artifact. Lesson: any tiny agent must read back the artifact (netlist/field/title bar), never its own text.

More steps do not fix a bad plan: two runs extended to a 500-step budget still failed at 467/488 steps. Lesson: don't buy capability with budget; the bottleneck is planning/perception/navigation (81% of root cause), not tokens.

Exact domain priors and canonical string forms decide pass/fail (LT3010 V_REF 0.808V; '2.8k' vs '2.80kOhm'). Lesson: tiny models need a small, exact domain-priors store; approximate conventions silently fail.

Integration cost is layered by runtime ownership: MCP is the default for existing harnesses, the in-process SDK when the product owns computer use, app-hosted service when a signed desktop app owns OS permissions. Lesson: for a headless ARM box the only $0 paths are the CLI (`cua-driver <tool>`) or a Python in-process SDK; Cloud Fleets is spend and must never be used without a Prime line.

Sandbox local mode depends on Docker/Lume/QEMU/Hyper-V; a 4-core ARM box without a VM/Docker path may be unable to run native providers at all. Lesson: verify the simulated (Playwright) provider first, since it is the only likely $0 headless path on this box.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Cua-Bench runs headless on this 4-core ARM box with the `simulated` provider and no VM/Docker/API key: a minimal task (click a button) completes and exports one trajectory whose `turn-00001/action.json` carries typed action records (tool name, args, result, observation).
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The simulated provider requires Docker/VM, a non-ARM browser, or a paid API key; or the exported trajectory lacks typed action records (screenshots/clicks only).
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: uv venv (py3.12) + pip install cua-bench; run `cb run task <minimal-simulated-task>` and `cb trace`; cat the resulting turn-NNNNN/action.json and list its fields. Record every failure verbatim.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The Cua-Bench trajectory record maps onto the town's jev typed-acts replay schema (action type, target, args, observation) with a <=20-line adapter, so a Cua trajectory is a usable typed-acts source rather than screenshots-only.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: action.json is free-text or screenshot-only, or the mapping loses action type/target/args/observation so the replay cannot reconstruct the step.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Parse one exported trajectory, write a 20-line field mapping to .agi/context/local-maxxing/typesafe/acts_replay.jsonl, count covered vs missing fields and name the gaps.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: At least one KiCad single-value-edit task (e.g. 84ec333e 'C1 -> 2 nF', frontier reward 1.0 in 50 turns) is solvable by a <=4B local CPU model through the Cua-Bench BaseAgent adapter at reward >= 0.5, giving a $0 verifiable computer-use signal on this box.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: No single-edit task reaches reward >= 0.5 at any step budget, or the local model cannot produce valid action calls through the adapter.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Implement a minimal BaseAgent wrapping a local <=4B GGUF via llama.cpp/CLI, run `cb run task <84ec333e-class task> --agent <name> --max-steps 60`, log reward/turns/failure_mode.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: $0; ~30-60 min (local-town or this box if a runtime exists)

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Cua Driver's per-action typed envelope {path, verified, effect, escalation} is a sufficient verification vocabulary for a tiny agent -- i.e. a kid can act on `effect`/`verified` without inventing its own self-verification, addressing the report's dominant failure mode.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The envelope is absent or non-discriminative on the Linux/ARM path, or `effect`/`verified` do not correlate with actual task success on the KiCad suite.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Read the Linux MCP tools reference and confirm the envelope is uniform; if an arm64 driver binary exists, run `cua-driver call get_desktop_state` and one action, and check the returned fields; else record the platform gap.
